title: Data Sentinel: logline sanitizer, tenant TTLs, and access ledger playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement a 'Data Sentinel' layer in the observability ingestion path that performs deterministic logline sanitization, per-tenant TTL enforcement for metrics/traces/logs, and an immutable access ledger for any read/unmask operations. The Sentinel should be extensible (rules + ML detectors) and support just-in-time reveal for debug workflows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingestion pipeline has a sanitization stage that strips or pseudonymizes PII from loglines and structured attributes for tenant-scoped streams. 2) Tenant TTLs are enforced for logs/metrics/traces and shown in Console retention dashboard. 3) Every access/unmask action is recorded in an immutable access ledger with actor, justification, and time. 4) Rollout gated by feature flag with canary tenant and no customer-facing incidents during canary. 5) End-to-end tests and synthetic traffic demonstrate <5% added CPU at peak and <20ms added median ingest latency for sanitized pipelines.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: build a hybrid sanitizer node in the Kafka/ingest layer. Use a lightweight rule engine (regex/schematized field masks) for deterministic removal plus a secondary ML classifier for fuzzy PII detection (email/SSN/credentials) to flag ambiguous lines for safe redaction. Store sanitized output alongside an audit token that references the original ephemeral blob in a zero-trust vault for JIT reveal. Access ledger will be an append-only record (signed events) stored in the observability metadata store with tenant scoping and retention matching legal policy.
tradeoffs:
- Regex/mask-first ensures low latency and predictable behavior but can miss edge-case PII; ML improves recall but is probabilistic and more expensive. We'll default to deterministic masking for production and use ML in a secondary asynchronous pass to surface missed items for re-processing.
- JIT reveal enables customer debugging but requires strict RBAC, justification, audit, and time-bounded tokens. Adds operational complexity.
- Enforcing TTLs at ingest avoids stale retention but complicates reprocessing/backfill; provide a migration path for historical data with a controlled scrub job.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged rollout in internal staging with synthetic tenants (2 days). 2) Canary deployment to 3 low-traffic customers for 1 week; monitor ingest latency, CPU, and QQ/rate errors. 3) Expand to 25% of tenants with automated rollback on error budget breach. 4) Full rollout after two weeks of stable canary and stakeholder sign-off.
- Ops hooks: dashboard for sanitizer false-positive/false-negative rate, audit-queue size, access ledger freshness.
- Backfill plan: idempotent re-sanitize job with rate limits and canary subset to validate behavior before large-scale run.
qa_and_testing:
- Unit tests for rule engine and ML classifier integration.
- Integration test that inserts known PII payloads and verifies sanitized output and audit token creation.
- E2E perf test with 10k rps synthetic load to validate latency and CPU overhead.
- Security review and pen test for JIT reveal flow.
- Compliance sign-off: data retention matrix updated and legal review completed.
metrics_and_dashboards:
Dashboards to create/update:
- 'Sentinel: ingest latency and CPU overhead' (median, p95, p99)
- 'Sanitizer recall/precision' (from sampled manual labels)
- 'Access ledger events by actor and justification'
- 'Tenant retention summary' (per-tenant TTLs, bytes aged out per day)
Links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Data+Sentinel+Spec, https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/sentinel-summary
runbooks_and_playbooks:
- Runbook: 'Sentinel incident triage' (how to rollback flag, how to rotate ML model, how to deny JIT requests).
- Playbook: 'Unauthorized access event' (immediate revoke, audit, customer notification steps).
Links: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/sentinel-incident, https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/sanitizer-v1.pdf
security_notes: Must integrate with KMS for ephemeral original blob encryption. JIT reveal tokens are short-lived (max 24h) and require multi-sig approval for tenant-scoped requests over threshold. Access ledger events are immutable and signed with service key; retention and searchability must be limited to authorized roles only.
